sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Leon County
sections.html:
The job is shared. A valuation office assigns parcel worth and approves exemptions, a collection office mails bills and takes money, and elected boards choose the millage that links them.

Sequence matters: values first, rates next, then a certified roll, and finally mailed notices. The collector cannot edit the roll, so a corrected name or address has to be requested from the appraiser.

  • Appraiser: values, exemption files, parcel data, owner records.
  • Collector: notices, payments, quarterly plans, delinquency, certificates.
  • Clerk: deed recording and the stamp tax paid with it.

Bills for each calendar year open for collection on November 1, and it falls to the owner to find out the amount before April 1. The 2026 bills were mailed in November.

Once April 1 arrives, the balance grows by a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, interest at 1.5 percent monthly and collection costs under s. 197.332(1). Delinquent names must be published in the newspaper within 45 days, and anything still open then is headed for a tax certificate sale on June 1.

The state discount ladder of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent, November through February, applies in Leon as elsewhere. With an escrowed loan, the lender should request the original notice from the collector so the owner gets a duplicate copy.

sections.h2: Installment plan for Leon County property tax
sections.html:
An estimated tax above $100 qualifies an owner for four installments. File the application with the collector before May 1; after that, enrollment continues automatically each year.

Leon County quarterly installment schedule
InstallmentDueDiscount and notes
FirstJune 306 percent off
SecondSeptember 304.5 percent off
ThirdDecember 313 percent off, plus half of any true-up
FourthMarch 31Full price, plus the remaining true-up

To get the discount, pay the first quarter by June 30. A late first payment is accepted through July 31 but at full price, and after July 31 enrollment is cancelled and the whole bill is due March 31. Quarters one and two mirror last year's notice, while new owners, values or exemptions affect quarters three and four. Selling mid-year? Hand the title company a record of payments made.

sections.h2: Exemptions through the Leon County Property Appraiser
sections.html:
March 1 is the yearly filing cutoff. The appraiser's site describes homestead and a group of veteran and service benefits; homestead comes first because the others depend on it.

Homestead in Florida comes in two tiers. The first $25,000 of assessed value is protected from all levies, school taxes included, and the second tier protects value over $50,000 from non-school levies alone. You must live there permanently as of January 1; leasing the home or leaving ends the benefit.

Each of the veteran and military exemptions the office describes requires homestead first:

  • A $5,000 reduction when a service-connected disability rates 10 percent or higher (surviving spouses may be eligible).
  • A discount percentage for combat-related disability at age 65 or older, matched to the VA rating.
  • Full exemption for total and permanent disability.
  • A deployment exemption, claimed with Form DR-501M and deployment orders.

Paperwork can be sent four ways, fax included. Income-limited senior exemptions may be added locally. Ask the appraiser what applies at your address.

sections.h2: How assessment caps work in Leon County
sections.html:
For non-school taxes, assessments on property without homestead cannot climb above 10 percent a year. Homestead growth is capped by Save Our Homes at 3 percent or inflation, whichever is smaller.

State caps have been 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. The sale resets the parcel to full just value on the following January 1, which means a buyer does not keep a long-time owner's low assessment. Remember this when setting a list price.

Amendment 3 starts January 1, 2027 and does not touch 2026 bills. The appraiser expects state guidance; watch that office's site ahead of the next roll.

Tangible personal property owned by a business is taxed separately from real estate and enforced differently. If it goes unpaid, the collector petitions for tax warrants; no certificate is placed on the land.

A month after the warrants are prepared, the office asks the Clerk of the Circuit Court for an order allowing levy and seizure of property, or garnishment of the delinquent taxpayer's bank account, for the tax and costs. Landlords with furnished rentals, or owners running a business out of a house, should know the same collector takes both real estate tax and this separate tax, with collection beginning each November 1. A seller asking for a payoff should ask whether any tangible account is tied to the address, and a buyer purchasing a rental from an investor should ask the same before closing.

sections.h2: Tax at closing in Leon County
sections.html:
Request a proration and a payoff number for any delinquent amount, and report installments you have paid. The agent splits the current year between buyer and seller, while late balances are paid out of your proceeds.

Deed stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, the same everywhere in Florida except Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk at recording, and all parties named on the deed are liable regardless of how they divide it.

On the settlement statement, look for the tax proration line and compare it with the collector's balance. If the numbers differ, ask the title company to explain before you sign. A balance paid at closing should come with a receipt or confirmation, and it is worth keeping that with your sale records.

The house loses its homestead on sale, and the buyer files again by March 1. A seller relocating in Florida can bring along the Save Our Homes benefit with Form DR-501T, filed within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead ended.

1. Get the current balance from the collector, along with word on any delinquent year or certificate.
  2. Check whether a business or tangible personal property account is attached to the address.
  3. A rented house means working around the tenant's lease, and renting ends homestead.
  4. Keep your latest notice and bill ready for buyers curious about carrying costs.
  5. Obtain a written payoff before agreeing on a closing date.

A cash sale cuts out lender underwriting, but title work still looks for tax balances, so the same steps apply. If a payoff changes between contract and closing, ask the collector for an updated figure and send it to the closing agent right away.

Tallahassee sits in Leon County, which counted about 299,048 people in mid-2025 over 668 square miles. Owners occupy only 52.6 percent of its 143,256 housing units, owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $301,800, and median gross rent is $1,291.

Since owners live in barely half the homes, plenty of sellers are landlords with tenants in the house. Homestead ends once a house is rented, and the lease can dictate the closing date.

faqs.q: When does Leon County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1 following the assessment year. After that the collector charges a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, monthly interest and statutory collection costs.

faqs.q: Can I pay Leon County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, when estimated tax exceeds $100 and you apply before May 1. The four dates are June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31; the first three carry 6, 4.5 and 3 percent discounts.

faqs.q: By when must Leon County homestead be filed?
faqs.a: March 1. The appraiser takes applications by email, mail, fax or in person, and will tell you the exemption amount.

faqs.q: Does Amendment 3 change my 2026 Leon County bill?
faqs.a: No. The amendment starts January 1, 2027, so 2026 bills stay as issued.

faqs.q: Who changes the name or address on a Leon County tax bill?
faqs.a: The appraiser handles it. Changes to the roll go through that office, so reach out before bills are mailed again.
